summary: A failed run is meant to stay deferred, but the periodic answered-wait and committed-resume scans call launch(), which unconditionally clears _deferred, so a poisoned run is retried indefinitely.
failure_scenario: A PARKED run has a stored reply. Its worker raises a non-OwnershipLost exception before any durable status or event change (for example a journal or claim-phase error). _report_failure adds the run to _deferred. The next pump tick (about every 0.25s) re-runs _scan_answered_waits, finds the same wait.event_seq and reply, and calls launch(). launch() reaches line 219 (or 198) and discards the deferral, so the run is started again. The same happens for a committed runs_resume command whose baseline is unchanged. The comment at line 93 says a fresh host or explicit operator action is needed to retry, but the scan is neither. The result is an unbounded hot retry loop and failure-sink spam.
evidence: Reproduced with a throwaway test (deleted afterwards) built on tests/api/test_run_host_recovery.py FakeJournal/FakeSystem. The run was PARKED with a stored reply, and _run_prepared raised RuntimeError. After 40 clock advances of 0.3s there were 120 attempts instead of 1. No test in test_run_host_recovery.py or test_reply_wake.py asserts deferral against these scans. Pre-existing; this commit only adds tests around the host.

summary: _start overwrites _tasks[run_id] while an older unwinding worker for the same RunId is still alive, and _fill_capacity never checks run_id in self._tasks, so the older task is untracked and survives shutdown.
failure_scenario: Worker A has persisted FAILED or PARKED but has not returned. A newer resume intent is queued behind it, and A's lease has expired or been released. _fill_capacity (lines 422-441) starts worker B for the same RunId and replaces self._tasks[run_id]. A is no longer in _tasks, so _abandon_local_state (line 244) cancels and awaits only B. A keeps running after shutdown(), which breaks the guarantee that shutdown abandons all local work. active_run_ids and the max_concurrency count also undercount live coroutines. test_older_worker_completion_cannot_retire_a_superseding_explicit_intent exercises the overlap but never calls shutdown while A is alive.
evidence: Reproduced with a throwaway test (deleted afterwards). With max_concurrency=2, two launches overlapped and 2 workers were started with 1 tracked. After host.shutdown(), the first constructicon:<run> task was still not done. Pre-existing.

summary: The 'no physical or provider call, guard kept' assertions in the process-restart test and the disposal_world fixture cannot fail, because the only code that touches the fake physical DB is unreachable.
failure_scenario: fake-physical.db is written only by forbidden_worker, which runs only if the RunHost starts a worker. The same script pre-populates host._deferred with every run (lines 31-35), which blocks ordinary recovery, so no worker can start. Nothing else in disposal reads or writes that DB. If runs_dispose_capabilities were changed to call a provider close(), reconcile() or guard release, test_real_process_disposal_restart_keeps_one_receipt_and_physical_guard would still pass, because `after == before` compares an untouched table. tests/api/test_capability_disposal.py::disposal_world uses the same deferral, so its `executions == []` checks are also vacuous. Only test_disposal_host.py's checks on _deferred, _requested and _tasks, and the provider-instrumented tests in test_capability_disposal_recovery.py, actually reach the guard.
evidence: Read the worker, the e2e test and the fixture. fake-physical.db is touched only inside forbidden_worker, and host._deferred is filled before startup. The mutation harness (scripts/check_capability_disposal_mutations.py) has no mutant for provider or physical calls. I did not run a mutant against this e2e test.

summary: _scan_committed_resumes restarts from after=None every cycle, so the whole runs_resume command ledger is re-read and re-decoded about every resume_retry_s, forever.
failure_scenario: After the cut is exhausted, lines 323-325 and 346-348 reset _resume_through and _resume_after to None. The next tick, 0.25s later, calls latest_command_key and then pages command_records from the beginning. Each page runs validate_command_claim_integrity. With N historical runs_resume commands, every idle host does O(N) decode work and a launch() per record continuously. Each launch is dropped later by the status or event-seq check, but it still does a journal.run_record lookup.
evidence: Source reading only. The cut is restarted and there is no durable watermark. The cost of validate_command_claim_integrity at scale was not measured.

summary: All 20 mutants in scripts/check_capability_disposal_mutations.py match their targets exactly once. Running the script gave KILLED for all 20 with baselines passing, so every kill came from an assertion failure rather than a harness error.
tests/substrate/journal/test_checkpoint_read_cost.py reaches its guard: one lookup decodes 1 payload through the patched _durable_model, so the early == late comparison is not vacuously 0 == 0.

AcquisitionClosure publish and commit use verified ref transactions with no-deref, closure-absence verification and candidate-value verification, so closure racing publication retries as a whole. dispose_acquisition uses finish_owned so cancellation cannot release custody mid-removal. No defect found.

_sqlite_capability_disposal absence proof (_project_disposal_receipt) checks the planned co-transactional lost slots when both audit and relationship are erased. A competing batch's transition is attributed through disposal_for_transition rather than treated as proof of absence.
